summary: Quick follow-up to last week's outage where Halo experienced elevated tail latency and a partial fallback to hosted models during peak batch jobs. We reviewed the interim mitigations (prefix cache bump, temporary autoscaler floor), validated RCA direction (KV cache expiry combined with an aggressive autoscaler downscale + longer compaction window causing increased cold starts), discussed short-term mitigations and longer-term reliability changes (dedicated capacity pilot, better autoscaler hysteresis, KV cache persistence options), and agreed on concrete next steps: run reproducible load tests, share logs, and schedule a 48-hour canary on Dedicated capacity. Customer had questions about SOC2, KMS, and SSO integration which we agreed to follow up with security docs.
topics: Root cause hypotheses: KV cache expiry + autoscaler behavior
Dedicated vs Hosted discussion and economics
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ben Gupta (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Halo SRE), Maya Rivera (Halo Eng Mgr), Samir Patel (Halo Head of Prod)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Ava: quick follow up to confirm actions after the incident, want to make sure the canary and logs are in place

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate) ---
00:00 Ava: ok uh thanks everyone for jumping on. this is the halo postmortem follow up, we have about 45 minutes, figure out owners and next steps. ben do you want to start with a quick recap of what we saw?
00:28 Ben: yeah sure, um so quick recap — on tuesday at 10:43 we saw a spike in tail latency, some requests fell back to the hosted fallback model, overall error rate stayed low but p95/p99 blew up for about 18 minutes. our preliminary trace shows a bunch of cold KV cache misses around the same time, and the autoscaler dropped nodes because CPU looked low so cold starts amplified.
00:55 Jordan: yep that's what we saw too, we had a big batch job at 10:40 that basically pruned a lot of prefixes then the KV cache TTLs expired and requests started hitting disk, disk reads added latency. also noticed more evictions than normal.
01:20 Maya: just to clarify are we sure the cache expiry was the start or was it the autoscaler timing, maybe both?
01:35 Ben: short answer: both. joint failure mode — TTLs + aggressive downscale. we think the autoscaler hysteresis was too tight, downscale interval was 60s and that overlapped with a period of low CPU because many requests were waiting on I/O rather than CPU, so nodes got removed.
02:05 Samir: and that triggered Redwood to route some traffic to hosted models? i thought that was a manual fallback?
02:18 Ava: no it was automatic once the Dedicated pool dipped below the threshold we had configured — recall we had a low-burst policy and an automatic fallback to hosted to keep latency bounded. the fallback kept correctness but not the SLA for latency, which is what you noticed.
02:40 Jordan: ok makes sense. we did see the hosted fallback but the integration was transparent to users, just bad latency.
03:10 Ben: quick note: some of the trace labels in the logs are garbled, the auto-transcription of the span ids got munged so we asked operations to re-export the raw traces, those will be attached to the S3 link Jordan will share.
03:36 Maya: question on mitigation — you mentioned a prefix cache bump, what exactly changed?
03:48 Ben: we bumped prefix caching TTL and forced a warm-up of the hottest keys by preloading during the incident window. also we set the autoscaler minimum floor to 2 nodes (was 0) to avoid full downscale during short-lived I/O waits.
04:12 Jordan: the floor definitely helped, after that p95 went back to normal, p99 improved but still slightly elevated.
04:30 Lina: i just want to capture that for the notes — temporary TTL bump + autoscaler floor + manual preload.
04:40 Samir: alright long-term what's the plan? we need this to not reoccur with monthly batch jobs, not just during our demo days.
05:00 Ben: long-term ideas: provision a dedicated capacity pool for the scheduled batch windows or move to a mixed strategy — dedicated for peak windows, hosted otherwise. improve autoscaler heuristics (use latency signals and i/o wait metrics not just CPU), make KV cache more persistent across restarts (store on faster local NVMe or warm from checkpoint), and add a better canary to detect cold-start cascades.
05:35 Jordan: can you elaborate on the KV persistence? we thought it was in-memory only.
05:44 Ben: currently it's in-memory with optional snapshotting. snapshotting has a small perf cost on write path so we disabled it by default. we can enable a periodic snapshot or a write-through to local NVMe to reduce cold start penalty. also we can prioritize warm-up for top-n prefixes.
06:15 Maya: cost implications? NVMe and dedicated nodes sounds expensive.
06:23 Ava: yes tradeoff — dedicated nodes add fixed cost but give latency predictability and avoid fallbacks. Redwood Optimize can show expected unit economics for your workload; i can share a short model.
06:40 Samir: we need numbers — if dedicated cuts p99 by 60% during batch windows how much extra monthly?
06:50 Ava: i'll send a simple TCO sheet, run the numbers for your peak schedule, should have by friday.
07:05 Jordan: security question — if we go dedicated, how does key management and logs work? we need KMS integration and audit logs for SOC2.
07:17 Ben: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and per-tenant audit logs. we also can host the private control plane in a VPC or on-prem if that is required. i will attach the security package with SOC2 report and details.
07:35 Maya: do you support SSO/SAML for team access?
07:40 Lina: yes SSO and RBAC are supported, we can show role mapping examples in the console demo.
07:50 Jordan: one more: during the incident we saw roughly 30% more cache evictions; is that a config we can tweak?
08:00 Ben: yes cache eviction policy has a few knobs — capacity, TTL, and compaction window. during that batch job compaction ran more aggressively. we can change compaction scheduling and bump capacity during scheduled jobs to reduce evictions.
08:30 Samir: ok so immediate mitigation is TTL bump + autoscaler floor + scheduled warm-up or dedicated pilot. what about observability — we need better alerts next time.
08:45 Ben: agreed. propose two alerts: 1) rising cold-miss rate for KV cache; 2) rapid node downscale event. both tied into slack pager. also add latency SLO burn alerts based on p99.
09:10 Maya: can those be sent to our pager duty?
09:18 Ava: yes we can integrate with PD, we'll include runbook steps in the alert.
09:25 Jordan: timeline for canary? we want to run during low-safety window then escalate.
09:33 Ava: schedule week of 10/25, run 48h canary on Dedicated with increased cache capacity during that window, Redwood SE will be on-call to watch metrics.
09:50 Ben: i'll own the reproducible test harness — i'll simulate your batch workload and the prefix churn. i want to share the test plan by 10/25.
10:05 Maya: we'll share the exact cron job and sample payloads, i'll get that to you by 10/21.
10:20 Samir: also want to review pricing for the dedicated pilot — can you send a proposal?
10:28 Ava: yes will send pricing and committed terms in the same email as the postmortem.
10:36 Jordan: on the logs — we have the LB traces and some of the model traces but we need guidance on what to redact before sending to Redwood.
10:44 Ben: share raw traces into a designated S3 bucket with encrypted access, for PII please redact user ids, we only need span ids, cache keys (hashed), and timestamps. we'll provide a script to mask sensitive fields.
11:05 Maya: good. security docs?
11:10 Lina: i'll attach the SOC2, penetration test summary (redacted) and KMS integration doc in the follow up.
11:20 Jordan: any competitors or alternatives we should consider? we evaluated ModelServeX a while back, Anthropic offerings were mentioned but not deployed — curious about tradeoffs.
11:33 Ben: general tradeoff is simplicity vs control. ModelServeX is simpler but less transparent on kernel selection and batching, Anthropic has strong models but you still need to manage inference economics. Redwood focuses on predictable economics and observability.
12:00 Samir: ok good. just ensure the SLA language for dedicated pilot matches expected uptime during our scheduled windows.
12:12 Ava: will include target SLOs in the proposal and a canary rollback plan.
12:25 Jordan: any blockers from Redwood side for the canary?
12:30 Ben: no blockers, we just need your logs and a confirmed schedule. SE will provision a dedicated pool and enable autoscaler hysteresis tweaks for the window.
12:45 Maya: thanks. small nit — we saw some transcription artifacts in the initial incident notes like span ids turned into words, can you re-export?
12:55 Ava: yes we requested raw trace export and will include the corrected ids in the postmortem.
13:10 Ben: quick technical detail — we recommend using latency-based autoscaler signal rather than CPU-only for your workload; we have an experimental hook to use p99-latency as a scaling metric. that would prevent node removal during I/O waits.
13:40 Jordan: that sounds promising, what's maturity of that hook?
13:46 Ben: it's been used by a few customers in beta, SE will run it in the canary and revert if it causes oscillation.
14:05 Samir: wrap up questions: how soon can we start the dedicated pilot?
14:12 Ava: can provision as soon as 48 hours after we agree to terms and you give log data. target start 2026-10-26 if we sign off this week.
14:30 Maya: ok we'll aim to get logs by 10/21 and internal signoff by 10/22.
14:45 Ava: great, i'll compile the email with postmortem, pricing, security docs and canary schedule.
15:00 Jordan: thanks everyone.
